localBiteReport: The most current reports available (week of Oct 30–Nov 5, 2026, roughly 3 days old) describe a productive but somewhat scattered fall bite around Choctawhatchee Bay and the Destin area. Redfish are the standout inshore species right now, schooling actively around bridges, jetties, and the East Pass, with guides reporting fish in the 25–26-inch class willing to eat a variety of live baits including pinfish, croakers, and herring. Speckled trout in the 22–27-inch range are also showing up wherever anglers can locate bait concentrations, though the bite has been somewhat unpredictable due to the disruption from a recent hurricane and a warm, unsettled fall transition that has kept fish between their summer and winter locations. Sight-fishing for reds on the Choctawhatchee Bay flats (around Hogtown Bayou and the tannin-stained shallows) has remained viable, with guides using quarter-ounce jigheads and paddle-tail soft plastics for reaction strikes. As daytime temperatures consistently drop below the 80s and overnight lows settle into the 50s, expect trout and redfish to stack up more predictably in the northern estuaries; water temp at this spot is measured at 75°F.
